saints.name: St. Irenaeus of Lyons
saints.title: Bishop, Martyr, and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: A disciple of the disciples of the Apostles, who defended the rule of faith against the Gnostics…
biography: Born about 130 at Smyrna in Asia Minor and reared a Christian, Irenaeus heard in his youth Polycarp of Smyrna, who had himself sat at the feet of the Apostle John, a living chain of two links from the Lord. Migrating to Gaul, he became a priest of the church of Lyons.

In 177, when persecution under Marcus Aurelius fell on Lyons, the imprisoned clergy sent him to Rome with a letter to Pope Eleutherius about the Montanist troubles; in his absence the aged bishop Pothinus was martyred, and Irenaeus returned to succeed him. His great work Against Heresies, written about 180, overthrew the Gnostic systems by appeal to Scripture, the rule of faith, and the succession of bishops from the apostles.

He pleaded about 190 with Pope Victor I not to cut off the churches of Asia over the keeping of Easter, and his writings are our earliest witness to the fourfold Gospel. He died about 202 and is honored as a martyr, though the manner of his death is unrecorded. In 2022 Pope Francis declared him a Doctor of the Church with the title Doctor of Unity.
saints.knownFor: His defense of apostolic tradition against Gnosticism.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; declared a Doctor of the Church in 2022
